name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q01 - SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature

questiontext.text: Which of the following represents the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature along with its standard symbol?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In the International System of Units (SI), seven fundamental physical quantities are chosen as base quantities, each having an internationally accepted base unit and symbol defined by the General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM).

Step 2: Identification of Base Unit and Symbol
According to the SI base unit definitions, the unit of thermodynamic temperature is the kelvin, denoted by the standard uppercase symbol \( \text{K} \). Other temperature units such as degree Celsius (\( ^\circ\text{C} \)) or degree Fahrenheit (\( ^\circ\text{F} \)) are derived or non-SI units.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature is the kelvin with the symbol \( \text{K} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q02 - Defining physical constant for kilogram unit

questiontext.text: In the revised International System of Units (SI) adopted by the General Conference on Weights and Measures, the kilogram is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of which fundamental physical constant?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The SI base units were revised in November 2018 so that each base unit is defined in terms of a fixed numerical value of an invariant fundamental constant of nature.

Step 2: Analysis of the Kilogram Definition
The kilogram, symbol \( \text{kg} \), is the SI unit of mass. It is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the Planck constant \( h \) to be \( 6.62607015 \times 10^{-34} \) when expressed in the unit \( \text{J s} \), which is equal to \( \text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-1} \), where the metre and the second are defined in terms of the speed of light \( c \) and the caesium frequency \( \Delta \nu_{\text{Cs}} \).

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The defining fundamental physical constant for the kilogram is the Planck constant \( h \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q03 - Atomic standard defining the SI second

questiontext.text: The SI base unit of time, the second (\( \text{s} \)), is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the unperturbed ground-state hyperfine transition frequency of which atom?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The standard unit of time is defined using a highly stable and reproducible atomic transition frequency.

Step 2: Identification of the Standard Nucliude
The second is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the caesium frequency \( \Delta \nu_{\text{Cs}} \), the unperturbed ground-state hyperfine transition frequency of the caesium-133 atom, to be \( 9192631770 \) when expressed in the unit \( \text{Hz} \), which is equal to \( \text{s}^{-1} \).

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The atomic standard used to define the second is the caesium-133 atom.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q04 - Defining physical constant for the ampere

questiontext.text: In the revised SI definitions, the ampere (\( \text{A} \)) is defined by fixing the numerical value of which constant?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The SI unit of electric current, the ampere, was redefined in terms of the fundamental electric charge carried by a single proton or electron.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Defining Constant
The ampere, symbol \( \text{A} \), is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the elementary charge \( e \) to be \( 1.602176634 \times 10^{-19} \) when expressed in the unit \( \text{C} \), which is equal to \( \text{A s} \), where the second is defined in terms of the caesium hyperfine frequency.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The fundamental constant used to define the ampere is the elementary charge \( e \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q05 - Nature of supplementary plane and solid angles

questiontext.text: In the International System of Units, plane angle and solid angle are physical quantities that have:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plane angle is defined as the ratio of arc length to radius (\( \mathrm{d}\theta = \mathrm{d}s / r \)), and solid angle is defined as the ratio of intercepted area to the square of radius (\( \mathrm{d}\Omega = \mathrm{d}A / r^2 \)).

Step 2: Dimensional and Unit Analysis
Because plane angle is a ratio of length to length, its dimensional formula is \( [\text{L}] / [\text{L}] = [\text{M}^0 \text{L}^0 \text{T}^0] \). Because solid angle is a ratio of area to the square of length, its dimensional formula is \( [\text{L}^2] / [\text{L}^2] = [\text{M}^0 \text{L}^0 \text{T}^0] \). Hence, both quantities are dimensionless. However, they are assigned standard SI units: the radian (\( \text{rad} \)) for plane angle and the steradian (\( \text{sr} \)) for solid angle.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
Both plane angle and solid angle have units but no dimensions.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q06 - Solid angle calculation for spherical cap

questiontext.text:
A spherical surface intercepts an area of \( 0.048\text{ m}^2 \) at a radial distance of \( 0.40\text{ m} \) from the apex center \( \text{O} \), as illustrated in the schematic below:

What is the solid angle \( \mathrm{d}\Omega \) subtended by this surface area at the apex?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Intercepted spherical area \( \mathrm{d}A = 0.048\text{ m}^2 \).
Radius from the apex \( r = 0.40\text{ m} \).

Step 2: Relevant Formula
By definition, the solid angle \( \mathrm{d}\Omega \) subtended by an intercepted area \( \mathrm{d}A \) of a spherical surface of radius \( r \) is given by: \[ \mathrm{d}\Omega = \frac{\mathrm{d}A}{r^2} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Working
First, calculate the square of the radius: \[ r^2 = (0.40\text{ m})^2 = 0.16\text{ m}^2 \] Next, divide the intercepted surface area by the squared radius: \[ \mathrm{d}\Omega = \frac{0.048\text{ m}^2}{0.16\text{ m}^2} = 0.30\text{ sr} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The ratio has dimensions of area over area, resulting in the dimensionless unit steradian (\( \text{sr} \)). The calculated solid angle is \( 0.30\text{ sr} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q07 - Definition of mole and elementary entities

questiontext.text: According to the SI definition of the base unit mole, which condition must always be fulfilled when using the mole to state an amount of substance?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The mole is the SI base unit of amount of substance (\( n \)). One mole contains exactly \( 6.02214076 \times 10^{23} \) elementary entities, which is the fixed numerical value of the Avogadro constant \( N_{\text{A}} \).

Step 2: Specification Requirement
Because amount of substance is a count of entities, the SI definition explicitly requires that the elementary entities must be specified. These entities may be atoms, molecules, ions, electrons, other particles, or specified groups of such particles.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The elementary entities must be explicitly specified (such as atoms, molecules, ions, or electrons).

answer.text: The measurement must only be performed on pure solid elements
The elementary entities (such as atoms, molecules, or ions) must be explicitly specified
The mass of the substance must be exactly equal to 12 grams
The substance must be an ideal gas at standard temperature and pressure

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q08 - Conversion of hectare into SI units

questiontext.text: The unit 'hectare' (symbol \( \text{ha} \)) is retained for general use to measure land area. What is its exact equivalent value in SI base units?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The hectare is defined based on the hectometre (\( \text{hm} \)), where \( 1\text{ hm} = 100\text{ m} = 10^2\text{ m} \).

Step 2: Calculation of Equivalent Area
One hectare is the area of a square with sides of length \( 1\text{ hm} \): \[ 1\text{ ha} = 1\text{ hm}^2 = (10^2\text{ m})^2 = 10^4\text{ m}^2 \]

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The equivalent value of 1 hectare in SI units is \( 10^4\text{ m}^2 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q09 - Standard atmospheric pressure in pascals

questiontext.text: What is the exact equivalent value of one standard atmospheric pressure (\( 1\text{ atm} \)) expressed in pascals (\( \text{Pa} \))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Standard atmospheric pressure is a conventional reference unit of pressure retained for general scientific and engineering usage.

Step 2: SI Value Identification
According to the standard conversion table for units retained for general use, standard atmospheric pressure is defined as: \[ 1\text{ atm} = 101325\text{ Pa} = 1.01325 \times 10^5\text{ Pa} \approx 1.013 \times 10^5\text{ Pa} \]

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The value of one standard atmospheric pressure is \( 101325\text{ Pa} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q10 - Relationship between bar and pascal units

questiontext.text: The unit 'bar' is widely used in meteorology and fluid mechanics for pressure. In terms of the SI unit pascal (\( \text{Pa} \)), \( 1\text{ bar} \) is equal to:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The bar is a metric unit of pressure, though not part of the official SI system, retained for general use.

Step 2: Value in SI Units
As given in the standard table of units retained for general use, one bar is defined as: \[ 1\text{ bar} = 0.1\text{ MPa} = 10^5\text{ Pa} \]

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
One bar is exactly equal to \( 10^5\text{ Pa} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q11 - Value of mass unit carat in milligrams

questiontext.text: The unit 'carat' (symbol \( \text{c} \)), commonly used in commercial trade of gemstones, is equivalent to which mass in milligrams?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The carat is a traditional unit of mass retained for general commercial use, especially for diamonds and precious stones.

Step 2: Value in Milligrams
According to the standard unit conversion table, one carat is defined as: \[ 1\text{ carat} = 200\text{ mg} = 0.2\text{ g} = 2 \times 10^{-4}\text{ kg} \]

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The value of 1 carat is \( 200\text{ mg} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q12 - Values of quintal and tonne in kilograms

questiontext.text: In standard commercial and industrial measurements of large masses, the values of 1 quintal (\( \text{q} \)) and 1 tonne (\( \text{t} \)) expressed in kilograms are respectively:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Both the quintal and the tonne (metric ton) are non-SI units of mass retained for general use.

Step 2: Evaluation of Values
One quintal is defined as \( 1\text{ q} = 100\text{ kg} = 10^2\text{ kg} \).
One tonne is defined as \( 1\text{ t} = 1000\text{ kg} = 10^3\text{ kg} \).

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The mass of 1 quintal is \( 100\text{ kg} \) and the mass of 1 tonne is \( 1000\text{ kg} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q13 - Definition of significant figures in measurement

questiontext.text: In reporting the result of a physical measurement, the significant figures (or significant digits) are defined as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Every physical measurement involves an experimental uncertainty determined by the least count of the measuring instrument.

Step 2: Definition of Significant Digits
By convention, the reported result of a measurement includes all digits in the number that are known reliably and with certainty, plus the first digit that is uncertain. These reliable digits plus the first uncertain digit are called significant figures.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
Significant figures comprise all reliably known digits plus the first uncertain digit.

answer.text: All reliably known digits plus the first uncertain digit
Only the digits that are completely certain
The total number of digits displayed after the decimal point

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q14 - Invariance of significant figures under unit conversion

questiontext.text: A measured length is reported as \( 2.308\text{ cm} \). When expressed in different units, it can be written as \( 0.02308\text{ m} \), \( 23.08\text{ mm} \), or \( 23080\,\mu\text{m} \). How many significant figures do each of these numbers possess?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The precision of a measurement depends solely on the measuring instrument and cannot be altered by merely changing the units of measurement.

Step 2: Application of Significant Figure Rules
- In \( 2.308\text{ cm} \), there are four non-zero digits and an internal zero: 4 significant figures.
- In \( 0.02308\text{ m} \), the leading zeros to the left of 2 are placeholders and not significant: 4 significant figures (2, 3, 0, 8).
- In \( 23.08\text{ mm} \), there are 4 significant figures.
- In \( 23080\,\mu\text{m} \), coming from the same measurement, the trailing zero arises from unit conversion and does not represent an extra measured precision: 4 significant figures.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
A change of units does not change the number of significant figures; all these representations have 4 significant figures.

answer.text: Different numbers of significant figures ranging from 4 to 5

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q15 - Significant figures in integers versus decimals

questiontext.text: Consider the two reported values \( 123000\text{ mm} \) and \( 0.06900\text{ g} \). How many significant figures are there in each value?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Rules for significant figures distinguish between trailing zeros in numbers without a decimal point and trailing zeros in numbers with a decimal point.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Number
1. For \( 123000\text{ mm} \): This is an integer without a decimal point. Terminal or trailing zeros in a number without a decimal point are not significant. Only the digits 1, 2, and 3 are significant, giving 3 significant figures.
2. For \( 0.06900\text{ g} \): For a number less than 1, zeros to the left of the first non-zero digit are not significant, but trailing zeros in a number with a decimal point are significant. Thus, the digits 6, 9, 0, and 0 are significant, giving 4 significant figures.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
\( 123000\text{ mm} \) has 3 significant figures, and \( 0.06900\text{ g} \) has 4 significant figures.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q16 - Significant figures in scientific notation base

questiontext.text: A measured distance is expressed in scientific notation as \( 4.700 \times 10^3\text{ mm} \). How many significant figures does this measurement contain?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In scientific notation (\( a \times 10^b \)), the order of magnitude or power of 10 is purely an exponent indicating scale and does not contribute to the precision of measurement.

Step 2: Analysis of the Base Number
All digits in the base number \( a \) are significant, including trailing zeros after the decimal point because they explicitly convey the experimental precision. In the number \( 4.700 \), there are four digits (4, 7, 0, and 0), all of which are significant.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The measurement \( 4.700 \times 10^3\text{ mm} \) contains 4 significant figures.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q17 - Significant figures of exact geometric constants

questiontext.text: In physical equations involving exact mathematical numbers or geometric definition factors, such as the factor \( 2 \) in \( r = \frac{d}{2} \) or \( 2\pi \) in \( s = 2\pi r \), how many significant figures do these exact numerical factors possess?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The rules of significant figures apply to experimentally measured quantities that carry uncertainty due to instrumental limits.

Step 2: Nature of Exact Factors
Multiplying or dividing factors that are neither rounded numbers nor experimentally measured quantities are exact. An exact number can be regarded as having an infinite number of significant figures (for example, \( 2 \) can be written as \( 2.0, 2.00, 2.000, \dots \) without introducing uncertainty).

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
Exact numerical factors have an infinite number of significant figures.

answer.text: The same number of significant figures as the least precise measured quantity

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q18 - Order of magnitude difference between Earth and atom

questiontext.text: The diameter of the Earth is approximately \( 1.28 \times 10^7\text{ m} \) and the diameter of a hydrogen atom is approximately \( 1.06 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \). By how many orders of magnitude is the diameter of the Earth larger than the diameter of the hydrogen atom?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Diameter of the Earth: \( D_{\text{Earth}} = 1.28 \times 10^7\text{ m} \).
Diameter of the hydrogen atom: \( d_{\text{H}} = 1.06 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \).

Step 2: Order of Magnitude Convention
In expressing a number as \( a \times 10^b \), if \( a \le 5 \), the number is rounded to \( 1 \times 10^b \), so the order of magnitude is \( b \). If \( 5 < a \le 10 \), it is rounded to \( 10 \times 10^b = 10^{b+1} \).
For the Earth: \( 1.28 \le 5 \), so order of magnitude = \( 7 \).
For the hydrogen atom: \( 1.06 \le 5 \), so order of magnitude = \( -10 \).

Step 3: Step-by-Step Difference Calculation
The difference in orders of magnitude is: \[ 7 - (-10) = 7 + 10 = 17 \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The diameter of the Earth is 17 orders of magnitude larger than that of a hydrogen atom.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q19 - Significant figures in density division calculation

questiontext.text: The mass of an object is measured to be \( 4.237\text{ g} \) and its volume is measured to be \( 2.51\text{ cm}^3 \). Express the density of the object adhering to the rules for significant figures.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Measured mass: \( m = 4.237\text{ g} \) (4 significant figures).
Measured volume: \( V = 2.51\text{ cm}^3 \) (3 significant figures).

Step 2: Relevant Formula and Rule
Density is given by: \[ \rho = \frac{m}{V} \] In multiplication and division, the final result must retain only as many significant figures as are present in the original measurement with the least number of significant figures.

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation and Rounding
Performing direct arithmetic division: \[ \rho = \frac{4.237}{2.51}\text{ g cm}^{-3} = 1.6880478\dots\text{ g cm}^{-3} \] Since the least number of significant figures is 3 (from the volume), round the result to 3 significant figures. The fourth digit is 8 (greater than 5), so the third digit 8 increases to 9: \[ \rho = 1.69\text{ g cm}^{-3} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The reported density is \( 1.69\text{ g cm}^{-3} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q20 - Decimal place rule for measured mass addition

questiontext.text: Three separate masses are measured as \( 436.32\text{ g} \), \( 227.2\text{ g} \), and \( 0.301\text{ g} \). What is the total sum of these masses reported to the appropriate precision?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass 1: \( 436.32\text{ g} \) (2 decimal places).
Mass 2: \( 227.2\text{ g} \) (1 decimal place).
Mass 3: \( 0.301\text{ g} \) (3 decimal places).

Step 2: Rule for Addition
In addition or subtraction, the final result should retain as many decimal places as are present in the measurement with the least number of decimal places.

Step 3: Arithmetic Sum and Rounding
Summing the numbers arithmetically: \[ 436.32 + 227.2 + 0.301 = 663.821\text{ g} \] The measurement with the least decimal places is \( 227.2\text{ g} \) with 1 decimal place. Therefore, round \( 663.821\text{ g} \) to 1 decimal place. The digit following 8 is 2 (less than 5), so the digit 8 remains unchanged: \[ \text{Total mass} = 663.8\text{ g} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The total mass reported to the correct precision is \( 663.8\text{ g} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q21 - Reduction of significant figures during subtraction

questiontext.text: Two lengths are measured as \( 0.307\text{ m} \) and \( 0.304\text{ m} \), both specified to three significant figures. What is their difference, and how many significant figures are retained in the result?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length 1: \( 0.307\text{ m} \) (3 significant figures, 3 decimal places).
Length 2: \( 0.304\text{ m} \) (3 significant figures, 3 decimal places).

Step 2: Principle of Addition and Subtraction
In subtraction, the result retains as many decimal places as the number with the least decimal places. Both inputs have 3 decimal places, so the result must retain 3 decimal places.

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
Subtracting the two values: \[ 0.307\text{ m} - 0.304\text{ m} = 0.003\text{ m} = 3 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m} \] In \( 0.003\text{ m} \), the leading zeros after the decimal point are non-significant placeholders. Only the digit 3 is significant, which represents 1 significant figure.

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The difference is \( 3 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m} \) (or \( 0.003\text{ m} \)), retaining 1 significant figure.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q22 - Surface area and volume of measured cube

questiontext.text: Each side of a cube is measured to be \( 7.203\text{ m} \). What are the total surface area and the volume of the cube to appropriate significant figures?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Measured side of cube: \( a = 7.203\text{ m} \).
The measured length contains 4 significant figures.

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
Total surface area: \( S = 6 a^2 \), where 6 is an exact number.
Volume: \( V = a^3 \).
By the rule for multiplication and powers, the final calculated area and volume must retain 4 significant figures.

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculations
1. Surface area: \[ a^2 = (7.203)^2 = 51.883209\text{ m}^2 \] \[ S = 6 \times 51.883209 = 311.299254\text{ m}^2 \] Rounding to 4 significant figures yields: \[ S = 311.3\text{ m}^2 \] 2. Volume: \[ V = (7.203)^3 = 373.714754\dots\text{ m}^3 \] Rounding to 4 significant figures yields: \[ V = 373.7\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The surface area is \( 311.3\text{ m}^2 \) and the volume is \( 373.7\text{ m}^3 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q23 - Total mass and difference of added pieces

questiontext.text: The mass of a box measured by a grocer balance is \( 2.30\text{ kg} \). Two gold pieces of masses \( 20.15\text{ g} \) and \( 20.17\text{ g} \) are added to the box. What are the total mass of the box and the difference in the masses of the pieces, reported to correct significant figures?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of box: \( m_0 = 2.30\text{ kg} \) (2 decimal places when expressed in kg).
Mass of gold piece 1: \( m_1 = 20.15\text{ g} = 0.02015\text{ kg} \) (2 decimal places in grams).
Mass of gold piece 2: \( m_2 = 20.17\text{ g} = 0.02017\text{ kg} \) (2 decimal places in grams).

Step 2: Calculation of Total Mass
Converting gold pieces to kilograms: \[ \text{Total mass} = 2.30\text{ kg} + 0.02015\text{ kg} + 0.02017\text{ kg} = 2.34032\text{ kg} \] Since the least precise measurement (\( 2.30\text{ kg} \)) is known only to 2 decimal places, the sum must be rounded to 2 decimal places: \[ \text{Total mass} = 2.34\text{ kg} \]

Step 3: Calculation of Mass Difference
Both individual gold piece masses are known to 2 decimal places in grams: \[ \Delta m = 20.17\text{ g} - 20.15\text{ g} = 0.02\text{ g} \] This result has 2 decimal places, consistent with both inputs.

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The total mass is \( 2.34\text{ kg} \) and the difference in the masses is \( 0.02\text{ g} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q24 - Rounding off numbers when dropped digit is five

questiontext.text: According to the standard scientific rounding conventions, what are the values of the numbers \( 2.745 \) and \( 2.735 \) when each is rounded off to three significant figures?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
When the insignificant digit to be dropped is exactly 5 (followed by zeros or nothing), the preceding digit is left unchanged if it is even, and is increased by 1 if it is odd.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Given Numbers
- For \( 2.745 \): The digit to be dropped is 5. The preceding digit is 4, which is an even number. Therefore, 5 is dropped and the preceding digit remains unchanged: \( 2.74 \).
- For \( 2.735 \): The digit to be dropped is 5. The preceding digit is 3, which is an odd number. Therefore, the preceding digit is raised by 1: \( 2.74 \).

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
Both numbers round off to \( 2.74 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q25 - Retaining extra digit in intermediate multi step calculations

questiontext.text: In involved multi-step arithmetic calculations, why is it recommended to retain one more digit than the significant digits in intermediate steps and round off only at the end?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In multi-step computations, premature rounding at each intermediate stage introduces cumulative truncation errors.

Step 2: Evaluation through Example
Consider the reciprocal of \( 9.58 \). Rounded immediately to 3 significant figures, \( 1 / 9.58 = 0.104 \). Taking the reciprocal of \( 0.104 \) yields \( 1 / 0.104 \approx 9.62 \), deviating from \( 9.58 \). However, if an extra digit is retained in the intermediate step (\( 1 / 9.58 = 0.1044 \)), its reciprocal is \( 1 / 0.1044 = 9.5785\dots \approx 9.58 \), successfully retrieving the original value.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
Retaining one extra digit in intermediate steps prevents the buildup of rounding errors.

answer.text: Because intermediate results must always have more significant figures than the final result
To convert derived units into fundamental units automatically
To artificially increase the precision of the measuring instrument
To avoid the buildup of rounding errors across successive steps

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q26 - Uncertainty in rectangular sheet area calculation

questiontext.text: The length and breadth of a thin rectangular sheet are measured using a metre scale as \( l = 16.2 \pm 0.1\text{ cm} \) and \( b = 10.1 \pm 0.1\text{ cm} \). Adhering to the combination of uncertainties rule, the area of the sheet should be quoted as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length: \( l = 16.2 \pm 0.1\text{ cm} \).
Breadth: \( b = 10.1 \pm 0.1\text{ cm} \).

Step 2: Relative Uncertainties
Relative uncertainty in length: \[ \frac{\Delta l}{l} = \frac{0.1}{16.2} \approx 0.00617 = 0.6\% \] Relative uncertainty in breadth: \[ \frac{\Delta b}{b} = \frac{0.1}{10.1} \approx 0.00990 = 1.0\% \]

Step 3: Combined Uncertainty in Area
Product: \[ A = l \times b = 16.2 \times 10.1 = 163.62\text{ cm}^2 \] Combined relative uncertainty: \[ \frac{\Delta A}{A} = \frac{\Delta l}{l} + \frac{\Delta b}{b} = 0.6\% + 1.0\% = 1.6\% \] Absolute uncertainty: \[ \Delta A = 163.62 \times 0.016 = 2.618\text{ cm}^2 \approx 3\text{ cm}^2 \] Rounding the calculated area \( 163.62 \) to be consistent with the uncertainty of \( 3\text{ cm}^2 \) yields: \[ A = 164 \pm 3\text{ cm}^2 \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The area should be quoted as \( 164 \pm 3\text{ cm}^2 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q27 - Relative error dependence on measured magnitude

questiontext.text: Two masses are measured with the same absolute uncertainty of \( \pm 0.01\text{ g} \). The first measurement is \( 1.02\text{ g} \) and the second measurement is \( 9.89\text{ g} \). What are the relative percentage errors in the first and second measurements respectively?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Measurement 1: \( m_1 = 1.02\text{ g} \), \( \Delta m = \pm 0.01\text{ g} \).
Measurement 2: \( m_2 = 9.89\text{ g} \), \( \Delta m = \pm 0.01\text{ g} \).

Step 2: Formula for Relative Error
The percentage relative error is defined as: \[ \text{Relative error} = \left(\frac{\Delta m}{m}\right) \times 100\% \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
For \( 1.02\text{ g} \): \[ \left(\frac{\pm 0.01}{1.02}\right) \times 100\% = \pm 0.98\% \approx \pm 1\% \] For \( 9.89\text{ g} \): \[ \left(\frac{\pm 0.01}{9.89}\right) \times 100\% = \pm 0.101\% \approx \pm 0.1\% \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The relative errors are \( \pm 1\% \) and \( \pm 0.1\% \) respectively.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q28 - Seven fundamental dimensions of physical world

questiontext.text: Which set accurately represents the symbols for the seven fundamental base dimensions of the physical world in SI?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
All physical quantities can be expressed in terms of combinations of the seven base quantities, designated as the seven dimensions of the physical world.

Step 2: Representation of Dimensions
In standard dimensional notation using square brackets, the seven fundamental base quantities are: - Length: \( [\text{L}] \) - Mass: \( [\text{M}] \) - Time: \( [\text{T}] \) - Electric current: \( [\text{A}] \) - Thermodynamic temperature: \( [\text{K}] \) - Luminous intensity: \( [\text{cd}] \) - Amount of substance: \( [\text{mol}] \)

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The seven dimensions are \( [\text{L}], [\text{M}], [\text{T}], [\text{A}], [\text{K}], [\text{cd}], [\text{mol}] \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q29 - Dimensional formulae of speed and acceleration

questiontext.text: What are the dimensional formulae of speed and acceleration respectively?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Speed is defined as distance divided by time, and acceleration is defined as change in velocity divided by time.

Step 2: Derivation of Dimensions
- Speed: \[ [v] = \frac{[\text{Length}]}{[\text{Time}]} = \frac{[\text{L}]}{[\text{T}]} = [\text{M}^0 \text{L} \text{T}^{-1}] \] - Acceleration: \[ [a] = \frac{[\text{Velocity}]}{[\text{Time}]} = \frac{[\text{L} \text{T}^{-1}]}{[\text{T}]} = [\text{M}^0 \text{L} \text{T}^{-2}] \]

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The dimensional formulae are \( [\text{M}^0 \text{L} \text{T}^{-1}] \) and \( [\text{M}^0 \text{L} \text{T}^{-2}] \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q30 - Dimensional formula of mechanical force quantity

questiontext.text: Force is defined as the product of mass and acceleration. What is the dimensional formula of force?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Relationship
\[ \text{Force} = \text{mass} \times \text{acceleration} = \text{mass} \times \frac{\text{length}}{(\text{time})^2} \]

Step 2: Substitution of Dimensions
Mass has dimension \( [\text{M}] \).
Acceleration has dimension \( [\text{L} \text{T}^{-2}] \).
Multiplying the dimensions: \[ [\text{Force}] = [\text{M}] \times [\text{L} \text{T}^{-2}] = [\text{M} \text{L} \text{T}^{-2}] \]

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The dimensions of force are 1 in mass, 1 in length, and \( -2 \) in time, written as \( [\text{M} \text{L} \text{T}^{-2}] \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q31 - Dimensional formula of mass density quantity

questiontext.text: Mass density of a substance is defined as mass per unit volume. What is its dimensional formula?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Relationship
\[ \text{Mass density } \rho = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Volume}} \]

Step 2: Substitution of Fundamental Dimensions
Mass has the dimension \( [\text{M}] \).
Volume has the dimension \( [\text{L}^3] \).
Dividing the dimensions: \[ [\rho] = \frac{[\text{M}]}{[\text{L}^3]} = [\text{M} \text{L}^{-3} \text{T}^0] \]

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The dimensional formula of mass density is \( [\text{M} \text{L}^{-3} \text{T}^0] \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q32 - Homogeneity of dimensions in kinematic equation

questiontext.text: Consider the kinematic equation of motion \( x = x_0 + v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 \), where \( x \) and \( x_0 \) are positions, \( v_0 \) is initial velocity, \( a \) is uniform acceleration, and \( t \) is time. According to the principle of homogeneity of dimensions, what is the dimension of each term on the right-hand side?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The principle of homogeneity of dimensions states that physical quantities may be added or subtracted only if they have identical dimensions, and each additive term must match the dimensions of the quantity on the other side of the equation.

Step 2: Dimensional Evaluation of Each Term
- First term: \( [x_0] = [\text{L}] \)
- Second term: \( [v_0 t] = [\text{L} \text{T}^{-1}] [\text{T}] = [\text{L}] \)
- Third term: \( \left[\frac{1}{2} a t^2\right] = [\text{L} \text{T}^{-2}] [\text{T}^2] = [\text{L}] \)
- Left-hand side: \( [x] = [\text{L}] \)

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
Each term on the right-hand side has the dimension of length, \( [\text{L}] \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q33 - Ruling out kinetic energy formula dimensionally

questiontext.text: Which of the following proposed formulae for kinetic energy \( K \) can be definitively ruled out on the basis of dimensional analysis alone (where \( m \) is mass, \( v \) is speed, and \( a \) is acceleration)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Kinetic energy has the SI unit of joule (\( \text{J} = \text{kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2} \)), corresponding to the dimensional formula \( [K] = [\text{M} \text{L}^2 \text{T}^{-2}] \). In any valid physical equation, every additive term must possess this same dimensional formula.

Step 2: Dimensional Analysis of the Expression
Consider the proposed expression \( K = \frac{1}{2} m v^2 + m a \):
- The first term has dimensions: \[ \left[\frac{1}{2} m v^2\right] = [\text{M}] [\text{L} \text{T}^{-1}]^2 = [\text{M} \text{L}^2 \text{T}^{-2}] \]
- The second term has dimensions: \[ [m a] = [\text{M}] [\text{L} \text{T}^{-2}] = [\text{M} \text{L} \text{T}^{-2}] \]
Because \( [\text{M} \text{L}^2 \text{T}^{-2}] \) and \( [\text{M} \text{L} \text{T}^{-2}] \) represent different physical dimensions (energy and force respectively), they cannot be added together.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The formula \( K = \frac{1}{2} m v^2 + m a \) is dimensionally inconsistent because it adds terms of different dimensions.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q34 - Dimensionality of arguments of mathematical functions

questiontext.text: In physical equations involving special functions such as trigonometric, logarithmic, and exponential functions, what is the mandatory dimensional requirement for the arguments of these functions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Special mathematical functions such as \( \sin(\theta) \), \( \cos(k x - \omega t) \), \( \ln(x) \), or \( e^{-a t} \) can be expanded as infinite power series of their arguments.

Step 2: Evaluation of Dimensional Consistency
In a power series expansion \( 1 + y + \frac{y^2}{2!} + \dots \), terms involving different powers of \( y \) are added together. According to the principle of homogeneity, quantities can only be added if they have identical dimensions. This requires each power of \( y \) to have the same dimensions, which is possible if and only if \( y \) is pure dimensionless quantity (\( [\text{M}^0 \text{L}^0 \text{T}^0] \)).

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
The arguments of trigonometric, logarithmic, and exponential functions must be dimensionless.

answer.text: The arguments must have the dimension of length
The arguments must have the dimension of time
The arguments must have the dimension of angle in degrees

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q35 - Dimensional correction in relativistic mass equation

questiontext.text: A student recalls the relativistic mass formula relating the moving mass \( m \) to the rest mass \( m_0 \) and speed \( v \), but forgets where to put the speed of light \( c \), writing \( m = \frac{m_0}{(1 - v^2)^{1/2}} \). Using dimensional consistency, what is the correct relation?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Incomplete Equation
\[ m = \frac{m_0}{(1 - v^2)^{1/2}} \]

Step 2: Dimensional Analysis of the Denominator
In the term \( (1 - v^2)^{1/2} \), the number \( 1 \) is a dimensionless number (\( [\text{M}^0 \text{L}^0 \text{T}^0] \)). By the principle of homogeneity, only dimensionless quantities can be subtracted from the dimensionless number \( 1 \).
The speed \( v \) has dimensions \( [\text{L} \text{T}^{-1}] \), so \( v^2 \) has dimensions \( [\text{L}^2 \text{T}^{-2}] \).

Step 3: Determining Placement of Speed of Light
To render \( v^2 \) dimensionless, it must be divided by another quantity having dimensions of squared speed, namely \( c^2 \): \[ \left[\frac{v^2}{c^2}\right] = \frac{[\text{L}^2 \text{T}^{-2}]}{[\text{L}^2 \text{T}^{-2}]} = [\text{M}^0 \text{L}^0 \text{T}^0] \] Thus, the expression under the square root becomes \( 1 - \frac{v^2}{c^2} \), making the denominator dimensionless. Consequently, \( [m] = [m_0] = [\text{M}] \), which is dimensionally correct.

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The correct relativistic mass formula is \( m = \frac{m_0}{\left(1 - \frac{v^2}{c^2}\right)^{1/2}} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q36 - Logical implication of dimensional consistency test

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements correctly summarizes the logical conclusion drawn from testing the dimensional consistency of a physical equation?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Dimensional analysis verifies whether the exponents of fundamental base quantities match on both sides and across all additive terms in an equation.

Step 2: Analysis of Test Outcomes
- If an equation is dimensionally inconsistent (fails the consistency test), it is definitely incorrect and physically impossible.
- If an equation is dimensionally consistent (passes the consistency test), it is not guaranteed to be exact or physically correct, because dimensional analysis cannot detect incorrect dimensionless numerical factors (such as \( \frac{1}{2} \) or \( 2\pi \)) or dimensionless parameters.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
A dimensionally wrong equation must be wrong, but a dimensionally consistent equation is not necessarily proved right.

answer.text: If an equation passes the dimensional test it is guaranteed to be physically and mathematically correct
Dimensional analysis can determine all dimensionless proportionality constants exactly
If an equation fails the dimensional test it is proved wrong, but passing it does not prove the equation right
An equation that fails the dimensional test may still be correct if suitable units are chosen

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q37 - Dimensional derivation of simple pendulum period

questiontext.text: The time period of oscillation \( T \) of a simple pendulum is assumed to depend on the length of the pendulum \( l \), the acceleration due to gravity \( g \), and the mass of the bob \( m \) as \( T = k l^x g^y m^z \), where \( k \) is a dimensionless constant. Using the method of dimensions, what are the values of \( x \), \( y \), and \( z \)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Relation and Dimensions
\[ T = k l^x g^y m^z \]
The dimensions of the quantities are: - \( [T] = [\text{M}^0 \text{L}^0 \text{T}^1] \) - \( [l] = [\text{L}] \) - \( [g] = [\text{L} \text{T}^{-2}] \) - \( [m] = [\text{M}] \)

Step 2: Equating Dimensions on Both Sides
\[ [\text{M}^0 \text{L}^0 \text{T}^1] = [\text{L}]^x [\text{L} \text{T}^{-2}]^y [\text{M}]^z = [\text{M}^z \text{L}^{x+y} \text{T}^{-2y}] \]

Step 3: Solving the System of Equations
Equating exponents of corresponding dimensions: - For mass (\( \text{M} \)): \( z = 0 \) - For time (\( \text{T} \)): \( -2y = 1 \implies y = -\frac{1}{2} \) - For length (\( \text{L} \)): \( x + y = 0 \implies x - \frac{1}{2} = 0 \implies x = \frac{1}{2} \)

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The exponents are \( x = \frac{1}{2} \), \( y = -\frac{1}{2} \), and \( z = 0 \), yielding \( T = k \sqrt{\frac{l}{g}} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q38 - Calorie magnitude in arbitrary system units

questiontext.text: A calorie equals \( 4.2\text{ J} \), where \( 1\text{ J} = 1\text{ kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2} \). In a new system of units, the unit of mass is \( \alpha\text{ kg} \), the unit of length is \( \beta\text{ m} \), and the unit of time is \( \gamma\text{ s} \). What is the numerical magnitude of one calorie in terms of these new units?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Dimensional Formula
Energy has the dimensional formula: \[ [E] = [\text{M}^1 \text{L}^2 \text{T}^{-2}] \]
The numerical value in the SI system is \( n_1 = 4.2 \), with base units \( M_1 = 1\text{ kg} \), \( L_1 = 1\text{ m} \), \( T_1 = 1\text{ s} \).

Step 2: Conversion Formula Between Systems of Units
In any two systems of units: \[ n_2 = n_1 \left[\frac{M_1}{M_2}\right]^a \left[\frac{L_1}{L_2}\right]^b \left[\frac{T_1}{T_2}\right]^c \] Here \( a = 1 \), \( b = 2 \), and \( c = -2 \).
The new units are \( M_2 = \alpha\text{ kg} \), \( L_2 = \beta\text{ m} \), and \( T_2 = \gamma\text{ s} \).

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution
\[ n_2 = 4.2 \left[\frac{1\text{ kg}}{\alpha\text{ kg}}\right]^1 \left[\frac{1\text{ m}}{\beta\text{ m}}\right]^2 \left[\frac{1\text{ s}}{\gamma\text{ s}}\right]^{-2} \] \[ n_2 = 4.2 \left(\alpha^{-1}\right) \left(\beta^{-2}\right) \left(\gamma^2\right) = 4.2 \, \alpha^{-1} \beta^{-2} \gamma^2 \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The numerical magnitude in the new system of units is \( 4.2 \, \alpha^{-1} \beta^{-2} \gamma^2 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q39 - Conversion of vehicle speed to covered distance

questiontext.text: A vehicle moves with a uniform speed of \( 18\text{ km h}^{-1} \). What distance does it cover in \( 1\text{ s} \)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data
Speed of vehicle: \( v = 18\text{ km h}^{-1} \).
Time interval: \( t = 1\text{ s} \).

Step 2: Conversion to SI Units
Convert kilometers per hour to metres per second using the conversion factor \( 1\text{ km h}^{-1} = \frac{1000\text{ m}}{3600\text{ s}} = \frac{5}{18}\text{ m s}^{-1} \): \[ v = 18 \times \frac{5}{18}\text{ m s}^{-1} = 5\text{ m s}^{-1} \]

Step 3: Distance Calculation
Distance covered in \( 1\text{ s} \): \[ d = v \times t = 5\text{ m s}^{-1} \times 1\text{ s} = 5\text{ m} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The vehicle covers a distance of \( 5\text{ m} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q40 - Conversion of gravitational constant to CGS units

questiontext.text: The universal gravitational constant has the value \( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}\text{ N m}^2\text{ kg}^{-2} \) in SI units. What is its numerical value in CGS units (\( \text{cm}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ g}^{-1} \))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Unit Equivalence
In SI units: \[ G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}\text{ N m}^2\text{ kg}^{-2} \] Since \( 1\text{ N} = 1\text{ kg m s}^{-2} \), the SI unit is: \[ \text{kg m s}^{-2} \cdot \text{m}^2 \cdot \text{kg}^{-2} = \text{m}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ kg}^{-1} \]

Step 2: Conversion to CGS Units
Substitute \( 1\text{ m} = 10^2\text{ cm} \) and \( 1\text{ kg} = 10^3\text{ g} \): \[ 1\text{ m}^3 = (10^2\text{ cm})^3 = 10^6\text{ cm}^3 \] \[ 1\text{ kg}^{-1} = (10^3\text{ g})^{-1} = 10^{-3}\text{ g}^{-1} \] Therefore: \[ 1\text{ m}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ kg}^{-1} = 10^6 \times 10^{-3}\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ g}^{-1} = 10^3\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ g}^{-1} \]

Step 3: Calculating CGS Numerical Value
\[ G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 10^3\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ g}^{-1} = 6.67 \times 10^{-8}\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ g}^{-1} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The value of \( G \) in CGS units is \( 6.67 \times 10^{-8}\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-2}\text{ g}^{-1} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q41 - Astronomical distance expressed in unity light speed unit

questiontext.text: A new unit of length is defined such that the speed of light in vacuum is unity (\( c = 1 \)). If light takes \( 8\text{ min} \) and \( 20\text{ s} \) to travel from the Sun to the Earth, what is the distance between the Sun and the Earth in terms of this new unit of length?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Speed of light in the new unit system: \( c = 1\text{ (unit of length) s}^{-1} \).
Time taken by light: \( t = 8\text{ min} + 20\text{ s} \).

Step 2: Conversion of Time to Seconds
\[ t = (8 \times 60\text{ s}) + 20\text{ s} = 480\text{ s} + 20\text{ s} = 500\text{ s} \]

Step 3: Distance Calculation
Using distance \( d = c \times t \): \[ d = 1\text{ (new unit s}^{-1}) \times 500\text{ s} = 500\text{ new units} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The distance between the Sun and the Earth is \( 500\text{ new units} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q42 - Linear magnification calculation from projected area ratio

questiontext.text: The photograph of a house occupies an area of \( 1.75\text{ cm}^2 \) on a slide. When projected onto a screen, the area of the house on the screen is \( 1.55\text{ m}^2 \). What is the linear magnification of the projector-screen arrangement?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Area on the slide (object area): \( A_1 = 1.75\text{ cm}^2 \).
Area on the screen (image area): \( A_2 = 1.55\text{ m}^2 \).

Step 2: Unit Conversion and Areal Magnification
Convert \( A_2 \) to \( \text{cm}^2 \): \[ A_2 = 1.55\text{ m}^2 = 1.55 \times (10^2\text{ cm})^2 = 1.55 \times 10^4\text{ cm}^2 = 15500\text{ cm}^2 \] Areal magnification \( m_{\text{area}} \) is given by: \[ m_{\text{area}} = \frac{A_2}{A_1} = \frac{15500\text{ cm}^2}{1.75\text{ cm}^2} \approx 8857.14 \]

Step 3: Calculating Linear Magnification
Linear magnification \( m \) is related to areal magnification by \( m_{\text{area}} = m^2 \): \[ m = \sqrt{m_{\text{area}}} = \sqrt{8857.14} \approx 94.11 \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
Rounded to three significant figures consistent with the input data, the linear magnification is \( 94.1 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q43 - Microscope magnification estimate of hair thickness

questiontext.text: A student measures the thickness of a human hair using a microscope of linear magnification \( 100 \). The average observed width of the hair in the field of view is \( 3.5\text{ mm} \). What is the estimated actual thickness of the hair?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data
Magnification of microscope: \( M = 100 \).
Observed image width of hair: \( w_{\text{observed}} = 3.5\text{ mm} \).

Step 2: Relevant Formula
Linear magnification is defined as: \[ M = \frac{\text{Observed size}}{\text{Actual size}} \implies \text{Actual size} = \frac{\text{Observed size}}{M} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Calculation
\[ \text{Actual thickness} = \frac{3.5\text{ mm}}{100} = 0.035\text{ mm} = 3.5 \times 10^{-2}\text{ mm} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The actual thickness of the hair is estimated to be \( 0.035\text{ mm} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q44 - Atomic volume of one mole hydrogen atoms

questiontext.text: Taking the atomic radius of a hydrogen atom to be approximately \( 0.5\text{ \AA} = 0.5 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \) and Avogadro constant \( N_{\text{A}} = 6.02 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1} \), what is the total atomic volume of one mole of hydrogen atoms?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Radius of a hydrogen atom: \( r = 0.5 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \).
Number of atoms in one mole: \( N_{\text{A}} = 6.02 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1} \).

Step 2: Volume of a Single Spherical Atom
Assuming spherical geometry: \[ V_{\text{atom}} = \frac{4}{3} \pi r^3 \] Substitute \( r = 0.5 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \): \[ r^3 = (0.5 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m})^3 = 0.125 \times 10^{-30}\text{ m}^3 \] \[ V_{\text{atom}} = \frac{4}{3} \times 3.1416 \times 0.125 \times 10^{-30}\text{ m}^3 \approx 5.236 \times 10^{-31}\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 3: Total Atomic Volume of One Mole
Multiply the single atomic volume by Avogadro number: \[ V_{\text{total}} = N_{\text{A}} \times V_{\text{atom}} = (6.02 \times 10^{23}) \times (5.236 \times 10^{-31}\text{ m}^3) \] \[ V_{\text{total}} \approx 3.15 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The total atomic volume of one mole of hydrogen atoms is approximately \( 3.15 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^3 \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_UNITS_AND_MEASUREMENT_MCQ_Q45 - Mass density of Sun and state comparison

questiontext.text: Given that the mass of the Sun is \( M = 2.0 \times 10^{30}\text{ kg} \) and its radius is \( R = 7.0 \times 10^8\text{ m} \), what is the average mass density of the Sun, and in which range of matter densities does it lie?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of the Sun: \( M = 2.0 \times 10^{30}\text{ kg} \).
Radius of the Sun: \( R = 7.0 \times 10^8\text{ m} \).

Step 2: Volume Calculation for Spherical Body
The volume of the Sun is: \[ V = \frac{4}{3} \pi R^3 = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times (7.0 \times 10^8\text{ m})^3 \] \[ R^3 = 343 \times 10^{24}\text{ m}^3 \] \[ V = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 343 \times 10^{24} = \frac{88}{21} \times 343 \times 10^{24} = \frac{88 \times 49}{3} \times 10^{24} = \frac{4312}{3} \times 10^{24} \approx 1.437 \times 10^{27}\text{ m}^3 \]

Step 3: Average Density Calculation
Average mass density: \[ \rho = \frac{M}{V} = \frac{2.0 \times 10^{30}\text{ kg}}{1.437 \times 10^{27}\text{ m}^3} \approx 1.39 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3} \approx 1.4 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The density of \( 1.4 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3} \) is comparable to the density of water (\( 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3} \)), which falls in the range of densities of solids and liquids, rather than typical gases.

answer.text: \( 1.4 \times 10^6\text{ kg m}^{-3} \), falling in the range of white dwarf stars
\( 1.4 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3} \), falling in the range of densities of solids and liquids
\( 1.4\text{ kg m}^{-3} \), falling in the range of densities of ordinary gases
\( 1.4 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg m}^{-3} \), falling in the range of dilute plasmas
